items.statement: Replacing the day 3 visit with a structured telephone review lowers the health service cost per trial episode, with no increase in unplanned attendances or 30-day infections.
items.rationale: Need is high because the pathway is changing anyway and the manager wants a costed answer; feasibility and parsimony are high because the data exist; novelty is modest.
items.risks: Year-on-year differences in case mix and staffing; small numbers for rare consequences.

items.statement: The change saves patients and companions more than it saves the health service.
items.rationale: Travel and lost working days are large (claim c4), while the service saving per episode is about one clinic slot.
items.risks: Patient costs before the change must be estimated from postcodes.

items.statement: Same-day reviews triggered by the telephone checklist offset most of the service saving.
items.rationale: A flagged call costs the call plus the clinic slot, so the trigger rate determines the saving.
items.risks: Trigger rates in the first months may not reflect steady state.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected as the service question, with h2 and h3 as named secondary analyses.
